topic.title: Scene Geometry from Sparse and Multimodal Observations
topic.overview: Scene reconstruction estimates depth, surfaces, occupancy, or motion from incomplete sensor observations. The represented work combines geometric constraints with learned priors, including monocular depth networks, radiance fields, foundation-model features, and information from different sensors. Sparse viewpoints make ambiguity central: several plausible scenes may explain the same images.
topic.whyItMatters: Better geometry supports navigation and spatial understanding, while self-supervision reduces dependence on expensive three-dimensional labels. Cross-modal guidance can compensate for weak measurements, but must account for differences in scale, visibility, and sensing characteristics.
topic.evolution: Early representatives study stereo disparity, transparency, and object recognition from views. Recent papers add sparse-view radiance-field reconstruction and semantic feature distillation; 2026 examples extend weak supervision to radar motion and heterogeneous perception. The shared concern is extracting stable geometry from imperfect evidence across changing sensor settings.
openQuestions: How should models represent geometry that the available views cannot determine?
Can auxiliary supervision transfer without inheriting another sensor’s systematic errors?
